description:
CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became: no EXEC PGM=CSUTLDTC exists anywhere in app/jcl or app/proc and the program is CALLed four times by two online programs (CORPT00C L392 and L412, COTRN02C L393 and L413), so it is never a Spring Batch job and is reached here as a plain object, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP layer in the path. LS-DATE='2022-13-15' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-DD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85); LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. The program declares no FILE-CONTROL and no FD, only WORKING-STORAGE (L22) and LINKAGE (L83), so it seeds no dataset, writes no record, leaves no dataset state and takes no job parameter - its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of the thirteen spans of 01 WS-MESSAGE (L42-L57), which sum mechanically to exactly 80, and are never captured from a COBOL run: no Language Environment CEE* service exists in this environment, so CEEDAYS cannot be executed at all. The pinned site is L139-L140, arm 6 of the ten-arm EVALUATE TRUE (L128-L149, WHEN OTHER last): FC-INVALID-MONTH is matched at L139 and moves 'Invalid month  ' at L140, a literal the author had already padded to fifteen characters with two trailing spaces and a lower-case m, reproduced byte for byte rather than stripped and re-padded. Severity 3 and message 2517 are DECODED from the halfwords 0x0003 and 0x09D5 of the 88-level VALUE X'000309D559C3C5C5' at L67, and never interpolated from the neighbouring arms: L66 carries 2513 and L68 carries 2518, so 2514, 2515 and 2516 do not exist. Month 13 is the UPPER out-of-range value and case12 drives the lower one with month 00; the pair is what stops a guard written only as 'month > 12', or only as 'month < 1', from passing, and the two cases differ in nothing but the echoed date span. 13 is numeric and fills its field, so nothing about the text's shape is wrong - that is what separates 2517 from 2520 FC-NON-NUMERIC-DATA, which case18 and case19 drive - and the month is rejected before the day is ever measured against a month length, which separates it from 2508 FC-BAD-DATE-VALUE, where the month is valid and only the day is impossible. It is equally not 2521 FC-YEAR-IN-ERA-ZERO, which case20 drives from a zero year: that arm is about the year, not the month, and conflating the two zero-valued rejections would collapse two deliberately separate arms carrying different message numbers. Because 2517 is not the 2513 that both callers single out and tolerate, CORPT00C and COTRN02C each treat this result as a hard error and paint their 'Not a valid date' message. The TstDate span carries an expected corruption rather than a defect to repair: L105 moves LENGTH OF LS-DATE, always the declared ten, into the S9(4) BINARY Vstring-length of WS-DATE-TO-TEST, and the group move at L122 then overwrites the clean date L107-L108 had placed in WS-DATE with the leftmost ten bytes of that group, so WS-DATE keeps the two-byte halfword and only the first eight characters. Here the offending month digits survive that truncation while the day 15 falls off the end, where in case07 it was the offending day that was lost. The halfword bytes 0x00 and 0x0A are binary and are written in this file as JSON escapes; they must not be confused with the month's ASCII digits 0x31 and 0x33, which are ordinary characters occupying the two positions six and seven bytes further on. WS-DATE-FMT is set once at L111-L113 before the CALL and L122 targets WS-DATE alone, so the mask span stays clean and echoes YYYY-MM-DD in full.

THE TWO CALL PARAMETERS, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. unitStimulus.linkage carries this case's whole input: LS-DATE = '2022-13-15' and LS-DATE-FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD', each written out to the ten characters PIC X(10) declares at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:84-85 with every trailing space visible - a mask longer than ten characters is TRUNCATED by the receiving field, and the truncation changes the message number, so the width has to be readable at the point the value is written. CSUTLDTC seeds no dataset and drives no screen, so these two values are the only thing a case varies; they used to live in a table in CSUTLDTCParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', which meant this file stated an eighty-byte result with nothing in it to say what was validated, and cases that differ only in their input were indistinguishable on disk.
